sn35.99:1.2: A bhikkhu who is concentrated understands things as they really are.
sn35.99:1.3: “And what does he understand as they really are?
sn35.99:1.4: He understands as it really is: ‘The eye is impermanent.’
sn35.99:1.5: He understands as it really is: ‘Forms are impermanent.’…
sn35.99:1.8: ‘Whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is impermanent.’…
sn35.99:1.9: “He understand as it really is: ‘The mind is impermanent.’…
sn35.99:1.10: He understand as it really is:
sn35.99:1.13: ‘Whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition … that too is impermanent.’
sn35.99:1.15: A bhikkhu who is concentrated understands things as they really are.”
